description.narrative:
The global objective of this call for proposals is to contribute to the empowerment of youth in Africa and to strengthen their involvement in active, meaningful and innovative ways.
The specific objective for Lot 2 AU-EU Youth Action Lab is: To create joint African-European youth-led cooperation activities that pursue long term impact and positive change. These should be supported by the award of small grants to innovative ideas in coordination with pilot dialogue and engagement mechanisms led by young people.
Nothing about us, without us. Oxfam Novib (ONL) together with the Oxfam International in Africa (OiA) team,have joined forces with Restless Development Uganda (RD) and the European Youth Forum (YFJ) to develop the AU-EU Youth Action Lab. This action addresses the lack of opportunities for youth in Africa and Europe to collaborate, cooperate, develop, implement and scale up their own initiatives. It is designed to support young people to be more engaged, empowered and connected, in line with the EU’s Youth Action Plan (YAP) and EU Youth Strategy. The action is based on the needs and priorities of young people as identified through extensive consultations conducted by the consortium members over the past four years. It is guided by our shared values and our experience in design and execution of inclusive grant-making programmes, and on learning from previous and ongoing initiatives. The action provides a unique safe and inclusive space for young African and European changemakers to connect andco-create, through the digital platform Power to Voices, which is designed for and with activists. It launches the AU-EU Youth Action Lab Fund to provide at least 110 grants that facilitate youth-led initiatives in Ethiopia, Kenya, Mozambique, Nigeria, Senegal, Sierra Leone,Somalia, Tanzania, Tunisia, Uganda, Zambia and Zimbabwe. This powershifting fund is co-designed by young people for young people, in such a way that they feel empowered to apply themselves, while their peers, assembled in the Youth Advisory Board (YAB), have decision-making power in the selection process. All grants bring young people together around a common identity or goal, and build on local assets, capacities and trust to facilitate complex change advancing young people’s rights and priorities.
To ensure a continental approach in Europe, European Youth Forum (YFJ)will engage with its existing network of youth organisations in all EU countries, who will be eligible to apply for Euro-African cooperation grants. YFJ will supportinter-continental cooperation initiatives with their diverse pool of trainers and mentors across their network. YFJ will implement their YFJ Academy model to provide a space where grantees part of the cooperation grants will gather and go through a learning experience on how to implement successful advocacy cooperation projects. Based on its geographical coverage and EU policy expertise, YFJ will build on its extensive existing youth network in Europe to strengthen synergies and support cooperation initiatives between youth organisations from Europe and Africa, focusing on policy advocacy. YFJ will oversee the Cooperation Grants.
